en: Vimānavatthu: The Chapter on the Woman’s Vimānas,
Section on the Seats (Pīṭhavagga)
9. The Story of the Radiant Mansion “O deity, you who stand there with such exquisite beauty;”
Illuminating all directions like a star among the herbs,
by what means do you possess such a complexion?
By what means do you succeed here?
For all those riches that are dear to the mind arise for you.
By what means, O deity of stainless radiance, do you shine so brightly?
By what means do all your limbs [possess such splendor]?
All directions shine with light.
I ask you, O goddess of great majesty:
what merit did you perform while you were a human being?
“By what means have you become so radiant in power, and why does your complexion illuminate all directions?
The deity, being uplifted in mind, [replied:]
Questioned by Moggallāna,
she answered the question asked,
[explaining] the fruit of that karma.
“In a former birth, when I was among humans in the human world,
I was a blind fish in the darkness.”
He gave a lamp at the time when a lamp was needed.
Whoever gives a lamp at the time when a lamp is needed in the midst of darkness and gloom—
I was reborn in a celestial mansion of radiant essence,
abundant with garlands and many white lotuses. Because of that,
my complexion is such as this.
By that, I succeed here;
and whatever wealth arises that is dear to my mind.
Therefore, O Vimalobhāsā,
I outshine you, O deity; therefore, with all my limbs, I [shine].
All directions shine with light.
O monk of great power, I tell you:
when she was a human being, she performed a double miracle of merit.
Thus I possess such blazing power,
and my radiance illuminates all directions.
Thus ends the ninth Vimāna, the Lamp Mansion.
